Let the rational roots of the first quadratic be \(-u,-v\), where \(u,v\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\). Then
\[
b=a(u+v),\qquad c=auv.
\]
The discriminant of the second quadratic is
\[
\Delta_2=(12b)^2-4(4a)(kc)
=144a^2(u+v)^2-16a^2kuv
=16a^2\bigl(9(u+v)^2-kuv\bigr).
\]
Thus we need
\[
9(u+v)^2-kuv
\]
to be a rational square for all positive rationals \(u,v\). Setting \(t=u/v\), this requires
\[
9(t+1)^2-kt
\]
to be a rational square for all \(t\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\).

At \(t=1\):
\[
36-k
\]
must be a square, so \(36-k=s^2\) for some integer \(s\ge 0\).

At \(t=2\):
\[
81-2k
\]
must be a square. Substituting \(k=36-s^2\),
\[
81-2k=81-2(36-s^2)=9+2s^2.
\]
For \(s=0,1,\dots,5\), the values are \(9,11,17,27,41,59\), and only \(9\) is a square. Hence \(s=0\), so
\[
k=36.
\]
Check:
\[
9(u+v)^2-36uv=9(u-v)^2,
\]
which is always a square. Therefore the only possible value is
\[
\boxed{36}.
\]
